  Review-only: do NOT edit any file. Act as the project's technical-director, adjudicating the Core ADR tier (Godot 4.7.2 GDScript, D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d). Files:
  - ADR-0011: D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0011-life-support-graph-data-model.md
  - ADR-0013: D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0013-ship-layout-block-geometry-and-id-allocation.md

  - ADR-0016: D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0016-restore-ordering-and-cross-block-verification.md

  Foundation (binding unless an amendment is truly needed): ADR-0001 tick driver/frame order; ADR-0002 authority/command pipeline; ADR-0003 block registry/owner contract; ADR-0004 change notification/dirty keys; ADR-0005 determinism/keyed RNG/encoding/hashing; ADR-0006 save container/generations/restore epoch; ADR-0007 static content pipeline/type ids; ADR-0008 render pipeline/integer scaling; ADR-0009 presentation subscriber contract; ADR-0010 source layout/typing/lint (all Proposed, in docs/architecture/).
  Cross-ADR items raised by the per-ADR reviews:
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0013: ADR-0013 says `LayoutGraphPort` (an `@abstract` port with `check_instantiate`, `instantiate_section(scope, ...)`, `opening_into`, `seam_openings_into`, `section_counts_into`) is 'implemented by the Graph's facade'. ADR-0011 names no class that `extends LayoutGraphPort`. `GraphView` is declared pure and getter-only, but `instantiate_section` is a mutator, and GDScript has single inheritance. The out types also disagree: ADR-0013 uses `SectionBases`, `OpeningRead`, `SeamOpenings` and `SectionCounts`, while ADR-0011 defines `InstantiateResult` and `WeldResult`. In the other direction ADR-0011 requires Layout to implement `RoomSource`, but ADR-0013 does not mention `RoomSource`, so `LayoutViews` may already have a base class. -> ADR-0011: add a file `src/sim/graph/graph_layout_adapter.gd` (`GraphLayoutAdapter extends LayoutGraphPort`) that wraps `GraphMutators` and `GraphView`, so the pure view keeps its contract. Rename `InstantiateResult` to ADR-0013's `SectionBases`, or alias it. Define `OpeningRead`, `SeamOpenings` and `SectionCounts` in 11. ADR-0013: name the class that `extends RoomSource` (a small adapter beside `LayoutViews`) and list `RoomSource` in its port section.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0012; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0012: ADR-0012 line 352 asks ADR-0011 to move `n_served` and `n_draw` (the `served_pm` basis) out of DERIVED into PERSISTED. ADR-0011 6.1, 7.4 and Alternative 7 say `served_pm` is derived and recomputed in `post_restore`. ADR-0012 also replaces ADR-0011 6.2 (4) (the `next` column swap) with accumulator apply, while ADR-0011 1 and 6.1 still describe `GraphScratch` as 'Jacobi next columns'. Both are data-model conflicts that change the payload and hash. The packed-array mechanics themselves are consistent. -> ADR-0011 to accept or reject the ADR-0012 request explicitly: if accepted, add the columns to 3.2 or 3.5, to the 6.1 PERSISTED row, to the size fixture and to the schema fingerprint, and revise Alternative 7. Update the GraphScratch wording to accumulators. The ADR-0016 phase-0 stock reconcile agrees with ADR-0011 7.3 (ADR-0016 4.3), so Open Question 2 can be closed.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0010; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0010: ADR-0011 says its accessors 'follow ADR-0010's naming rule (no get, set, free, call)'. ADR-0010 line 146 words the rule as 'accessors are named `get_<noun>` or `lookup`, never `get`, `set`, ...'. Read literally, `served_pm(id)`, `node_state(id)` and `step_no()` do not follow it. ADR-0017 and ADR-0034 already call those names. Separately, ADR-0011 asks ADR-0010 to name `mini`/`maxi`/`clampi`/`absi`/`signi` as permitted under SIM-04 (foundation ask 2). I confirmed the typed builtins exist and return int. I also confirmed that `can_instantiate()` returns true for an `@abstract` class (RoomSource), so the ADR-0010 load_all gate (which fails on `can_instantiate()` false) will not reject ports. -> ADR-0010: reword the accessor rule as 'never the exact names get/set/free/call/...; a `get_` prefix is optional', or ADR-0011 adopts `get_` names (which would ripple into ADR-0017 and ADR-0034). Add the typed numeric builtins to the SIM-04 allow-list. Add `static var` in persisted-state classes to OWN-01 (E2).
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0011; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0012, ADR-0017: Persisted hook products. ADR-0012 § 11 requires `n_served`, `n_draw` and CABLE `e0` net load to be persisted for restore equivalence on any tick. ADR-0017 depends on `served_pm` being exact after restore. ADR-0011 currently classes `served_pm` as DERIVED and rejects persisting it (Alternative 7). The column decision is ADR-0011's. -> ADR-0011 adopts the three columns per finding T1 and updates the size to about 30.5 KB. ADR-0012 § 11 and ADR-0017 then drop their conditional 'if ADR-0011 declines' fallback text.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0012; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0012, ADR-0017: `last_step_no` meaning. ADR-0012 § 1 owns the hook cursors and defines `last_step_no` as the step whose failure hook completed (LS-8). ADR-0017's FAULT_GLOW reconcile and FT-15 depend on that meaning. ADR-0011 § 2.3 says 'power hook'. ADR-0011 is the amender, not the owner. -> ADR-0011 § 2.3, § 3.8 and the `GraphView.last_step_no()` comment adopt ADR-0012 § 1's definition verbatim (finding T2).
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0011; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0012, ADR-0010: Graph writer-file matrix and the OWN-01 configuration. ADR-0011 § 12.1 names a single `graph_propagate.gd` and makes GraphCaches writable only by `graph_derived.gd`. ADR-0012 has a `propagate/` directory, writes caches in phases 7 and 11, updates last-emitted buckets from mutators, and sizes scratch from the derived file. ADR-0010 must accept directory globs in `field_writers.json`. -> ADR-0011 publishes one per-class writer matrix (finding T3) and merges ADR-0012 Foundation Ask 1 (glob support) into its own Foundation Ask 1 to ADR-0010. ADR-0012's Key Interfaces comment then cites ADR-0011 § 12.1 instead of restating the set.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0011, ADR-0012: `LayoutGraphPort` and the M1 call chain. ADR-0013 § 8 defines the port: `check_instantiate`, `instantiate_section(..., out: SectionBases)`, `opening_into`, `seam_openings_into`, `section_counts_into`. It routes M1 as Web Map `init_world` → LM1 → port, so that Layout allocates `section_id` first. ADR-0011 implements none of the reads, names the out type `InstantiateResult`, and (with ADR-0012 § 6) says Web Map calls M1 directly. ADR-0013 owns the port definition; ADR-0011 is the implementer. -> ADR-0011 adds the facade `extends LayoutGraphPort` with all five methods (finding T4) and adopts one out-type name; whichever name is chosen, ADR-0013 and ADR-0011 must match. ADR-0011 § 1 and ADR-0012 § 6 (M1 row and Rules) reword M1's caller as 'Layout LM1 through LayoutGraphPort, itself called only by Web Map `init_world` in the INIT scope'. ADR-0013 § 3's table fixes two wording errors: there is no 'comp counter' (cid is the COMPARTMENT node id, from `next_node_id`), and opening ids are edge ids from `next_edge_id`, not from `next_seam_id`.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0011; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0012, ADR-0016: Hook-cursor restore verification. ADR-0012 assigns it to ADR-0016's verifier, but ADR-0016 has no cursor check; its V3 row delegates to ADR-0011 § 7.2. The Graph's fault table and restore precedence are ADR-0011's. -> ADR-0011 appends `HOOK_CURSOR` (25) and `RESTORE_CURSOR` (26) and adds a § 7.2 step that checks each cursor against the clock installed at ADR-0016 R2 (finding T5). ADR-0012 § 1 changes its cross-ADR note from ADR-0016 to ADR-0011 § 7.2. ADR-0016's V3 text ('the ordered steps of ADR-0011 § 7.2') then covers it without change.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0011; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0017: Stale-id read sentinel. ADR-0017 assumes `GraphView` getters return a not-live sentinel for an unknown or tombstoned id. ADR-0011 § 4.1 (5) says 'neutral value', which for `node_state` is 0 (OK). -> ADR-0011 defines per-getter sentinels or `node_live`/`edge_live` guards (finding T6). ADR-0017 cites them by name.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0012; adrs ADR-0012, ADR-0011: Contents of GraphScratch. ADR-0012 § 3 replaces ADR-0011 § 6.2 (4)'s Jacobi `next` columns with delta accumulators (JAC discipline), so at MVP GraphScratch holds accumulators and traversal buffers only. ADR-0011 § 1, § 6.1 and § 6.2 still describe `next` columns. -> ADR-0011 § 1 table, § 6.1 SCRATCH row and § 6.2 (4) say: 'GraphScratch holds the ADR-0012 § 3 inventory (accumulators, island, candidate, sort and traversal buffers), all-zero at every hook exit; the swap-by-reference rule stays available for a future wholesale-rewritten field'.
  [from ADR-0011 review] owner ADR-0016; adrs ADR-0016, ADR-0011: ADR-0016's Tier S list cites the Graph 'step_no (from hdr)' for Suit V7 and Interaction V10 decoding. ADR-0011 § 2.3 defines `step_no()` as `floor_div(clock.tick(), GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`, which is valid once ADR-0016 R2 installs the clock. The hdr holds only cursors, which may trail by up to one step (T2), so 'from hdr' would give a different number. -> ADR-0016 rewords the Tier S entry to 'GraphView.step_no() (derived from the installed kernel clock at R2, not from hdr)'. ADR-0011 needs no change beyond T2.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0011; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0011: ADR-0013 § 8 defines the Graph-side port `LayoutGraphPort` (check_instantiate, instantiate_section(..., out: SectionBases), opening_into, seam_openings_into, section_counts_into) and says the Graph's facade `extends LayoutGraphPort`. ADR-0011 never mentions `LayoutGraphPort`. It names M1's out object `InstantiateResult {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` and defines only `RoomSource` as a port. The helper record types `SectionBases`, `OpeningRead`, `SeamOpenings` and `SectionCounts` are defined in neither ADR. GDScript allows one superclass, so the Graph facade can extend `LayoutGraphPort` only if it is a dedicated adapter class, not `GraphModule`. -> ADR-0011 should add the dedicated adapter (for example `GraphLayoutPort extends LayoutGraphPort`, in `src/sim/graph/`), rename M1's out type to match or alias `SectionBases`, and define `OpeningRead`, `SeamOpenings` and `SectionCounts` as caller-owned records with preallocated packed buffers. Both ADRs must pick one owner for those four types (ADR-0013 proposes `src/sim/layout/ports/`). Until then ADR-0013 R7 stays open.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0011, ADR-0014, ADR-0015: ADR-0011 says `RoomSource` (room_volume_tiles, room_exposed_tiles) is implemented by "Layout's read view". ADR-0014 uses separate adapters `LayoutSolidQuery extends SolidQuery` and `LayoutOccluderSource extends OccluderSource`, and ADR-0015 uses `LayoutCollide extends CollideSource` and a `BodyLayoutPort` adapter over `LayoutViews`. GDScript single inheritance means `LayoutViews` can extend at most one port, and ADR-0013 § 11 does not say which, or that it extends none. ADR-0013 also exposes `version`, `static_version`, `leaf_version`, `changed_region_*` and `V` directly on `LayoutViews`, while ADR-0014's `OccluderSource` declares `version/static_version/leaf_version/changed_region_*` and ADR-0011 asks for `room_volume_tiles`. -> ADR-0013 § 11 should state that `LayoutViews` extends `RefCounted` only, that each port is satisfied by a small adapter class in `src/sim/layout/` that delegates to it (a `LayoutRoomSource extends RoomSource` is missing from the list), and that the adapter method names are the ports' (so `room_volume_tiles` wraps `V`). Add `LayoutRoomSource` to the module source layout in § 1 and to the composition-root injection list.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0010; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0010: ADR-0010 line 148 records as UNVERIFIED whether an `@abstract` method's parameters trigger UNUSED_PARAMETER. Probed on 4.7.2 with `unused_parameter=2`: the abstract declarations do not fire (including a trailing comment, a one-line `@abstract class_name`, and a StringName return); implementations that do not use a parameter do fire and need a `_` prefix, and the renamed override still loads. This also means the `class_name` header may sit on the `@abstract` line, which ADR-0011 uses and ADR-0010 writes on two lines. -> ADR-0010 should close the UNVERIFIED with this result (LINT-SPIKE-1(b)) and add the convention "implementations and doubles of a port prefix unused parameters with `_`". Port files under `ports/` may use either `@abstract` placement; pick one for the lexical `ARCH-05` check so it does not miss the one-line form.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0006; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0006: ADR-0006 § 1.2 and the probe row say typed `Array[T]`/`Dictionary[K,V]` round-trip their values and "type preservation is not asserted [70%]". ADR-0013 relies on a typed `Array[String]` template_id column and states it "survives still typed". Reproduced on 4.7.2: `var_to_bytes` then `bytes_to_var` of a Dictionary holding an `Array[String]` returns a typed array (is_typed true, get_typed_builtin TYPE_STRING), and `duplicate(true)` keeps it typed. Not covered: JSON-decoded or other-path data. -> ADR-0006 can upgrade claim (5) for `Array[String]` to "preserved through var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var and duplicate(true), probed 2026-10-29 (reviewer)" while keeping the rule that owners must not depend on it. ADR-0013 restore must fill typed columns with `Array[String].assign(...)` after a per-element `typeof` check (see E5).
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0010; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0010: ADR-0013 R4/Validation lean on `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` for allocation-free hot reads. ADR-0010 P6/P7/CNT-01 already record that OBJECT_COUNT counts Objects only and MEMORY_STATIC is blind to transient allocation, so HOT-01 is the only check of packed-array, Array, Dictionary and string allocation in the Layout Tier H reads. No contradiction, but the dependency is one-way: HOT-01's tag list in ADR-0010 must name the Layout Tier H functions and the `layout.doors` hook body. -> ADR-0010 § 6.6 tag list: add `LayoutViews.room_at`, `floor_tile_at`, `section_at`, `body_of`, `door_passage_into`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `leaf_obstruction_into`, `exposed_tiles`, `V` and the `layout.doors` hook body. ADR-0013 E9 wording change as above.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0006, ADR-0016: The drift-policy hash rewrite in Layout restore() has no REBASED cause in ADR-0006's closed set of five. ADR-0016 section 9.3 says it is 'accepted as a REBASED case' without naming one. -> ADR-0013 removes the rewrite from restore() and refreshes the hashes in LM2 (T1). ADR-0016 section 9.3 then replaces its sentence with 'layout.state restore is byte-identical; content drift is diagnostic only'. ADR-0006 needs no change.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0011; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0013: No implementer of LayoutGraphPort exists. ADR-0011 publishes no opening_into, seam_openings_into, section_counts_into or check_instantiate/LayoutGraphPort facade. It has GraphView.opening_area, seam_view and InstantiateResult instead. -> ADR-0011 adds to its Key Interfaces a Graph-side adapter that extends LayoutGraphPort (allocation-free opening_into, seam_openings_into in socket_plan.openings order, section_counts_into, check_instantiate_section, instantiate_section with InstantiateResult), valid in the APPLY, INIT, HOOK and post_restore phases.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0011; adrs ADR-0011, ADR-0013, ADR-0016: RAGGED-cut stub HULL_SEGMENT rows and discard tombstones fall outside or within a section's contiguous M1 range in ways that section_counts_into does not define. Layout's post-restore check (d), ADR-0016's verifier V2 and the reverse id-to-section lookup depend on that definition. -> ADR-0011 defines section_counts_into's out as template-range counts (nodes, edges, compartments created by M1) plus a separate stub_count, with tombstone status reported, and states that a stub's section_of is the cut section. ADR-0013 (T2) adjusts its check and its reverse lookup to match.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0011: Setup cycle: Layout is set up first and needs LayoutGraphPort, while the Graph's setup needs Layout's RoomSource. ADR-0013 does not declare RoomSource. -> ADR-0013 constructs LayoutViews in setup, implements RoomSource, exposes room_source(), and adds bind_graph(port) called after GraphModule.setup and before the freeze (T3). architecture.md section 8 notes the binding step.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0034; adrs ADR-0014, ADR-0034, ADR-0013: ADR-0034's assumption says section_rects_into rows carry the extent 'in section-local px', but ADR-0014 section 5 defines section_rects_into as answering in the body frame, with occupied spans (x1 - 1, y1 - 1). -> ADR-0034 restates its assumption to body-frame occupied spans and converts by subtracting section_offset when it builds section-parented sprites. ADR-0013 lists the exception in its frame rule (T5).
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0034: JAMB is missing from ADR-0013's closed kind_ordinal vocabulary. ADR-0034 assigns JAMB 7 (OQ-C). -> ADR-0013 section 13 adds JAMB (T6). ADR-0034 then closes OQ-C.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0014: ADR-0014 replaces LM4's version bump with invalidate (counters set to 0) and adds version_epoch as the restore signal. ADR-0013's sections 9 and 10 do not reflect either. -> ADR-0013 adopts invalidate on discard and new_epoch() on restore/default_state, and cites version_epoch (T7).
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0015, ADR-0017: Reads that siblings consume are not published in ADR-0013 section 11: body_is_live and section_contains (ADR-0015), node_base(section_id) and template emitter placements (ADR-0017), the RectFlags file and the SlotFeed (ADR-0014). -> ADR-0013 section 11 adds a 'Reads owed to Core siblings' table with signatures and tiers (T5).
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0003; adrs ADR-0003, ADR-0013, ADR-0015: The Class A pure check is named check_* in ADR-0003 section 5 and the registry, while Layout keeps the GDD-published can_* names with the identical shape. -> ADR-0003 amends section 5 to 'a pure check, conventionally check_*; an owner may keep a GDD-published can_* name with the same shape', so the registry stance mutator_status admits both.
  [from ADR-0013 review] owner ADR-0013; adrs ADR-0013, ADR-0011, ADR-0021: Weld argument-order independence is guaranteed for layout.state only. JoinPlan is filled in caller argument order, so graph.state seam rows can differ between attach(x, y) and attach(y, x). -> ADR-0013's socket_plan canonicalises survivor-first (T9). ADR-0021's weld property test asserts whole-world state_hash equality for reversed arguments.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0001; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0001, ADR-0009: ADR-0001 § 3 item 3b says `_input` / `_unhandled_input` are delivered before the frame's `_process` (UNVERIFIED), and ADR-0009's INPUT_SURFACE rule says a holder latches intents from events. Probed on 4.7.2 headless: `_input` is delivered before `_process` with press/release order preserved (confirmed), but `_input` order among nodes is reverse tree order and ignores `process_priority`. A later-in-tree node that handles an event starves the Adapter's ring. ADR-0001 § 3 and ADR-0009 imply that priority governs the Adapter's whole input path. -> ADR-0001 § 3: mark 3b probed (headless), add 'process_priority orders `_process` only; `_input` order is reverse tree order'. ADR-0009 INPUT_SURFACE rule: the composition root adds each INPUT_SURFACE object as the last child of the root, and no other node calls `set_input_as_handled()` on action-bound events.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0015; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0015: ADR-0019 § 1.1 lists a 'pod-body test' among the Controller's reads of `body.state`, and § 6.1 reads `pos_curr` as a `Vector2i` from Body's published view. ADR-0015 publishes scalar getters (`pos_x`, `pos_y`, `prev_x`, `prev_y`, `body_of_actor`, `seat_of_actor`, `actor_of_seat`, ...) and states the pod-body test is Layout's or Transit's, not Body's. Not engine-specific, but the call shapes do not exist as written. -> ADR-0019 reads `pos_x` / `pos_y` (or builds the `Vector2i` once at the Adapter boundary) and sources the pod-body test from the owner ADR-0015 names. ADR-0015 confirms the getter names in its Key Interfaces.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0030; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0030, ADR-0031: ADR-0030 (forward reference) builds the Chart Table layer and ADR-0031 the debug overlay. If either node sits later in the tree and receives keyboard, mouse or pad events through its own `_input`, `_gui_input` or `ui_*` actions, it takes the event before the Adapter (E2). A focused Control will also act on `ui_accept` / `ui_cancel`, which exist in the default InputMap regardless of the Adapter. ADR-0019 R4 and OQ-B only note a possible collision. -> ADR-0030 and ADR-0031 state: no `_input` or `set_input_as_handled()` in their layers; they consume MenuInput and `DevInputSink` through the Adapter; Controls in the layer set `focus_mode` NONE (or are exempted through the TextEntryProbe port of OQ-B).
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0019; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0017, ADR-0018: The chest point (beam apex) is computed in controller.step before body.integrate, while emitter.place reads it alongside the post-integrate pos_curr as the occlusion origin, so the two are one tick apart while the avatar moves. The frame, the CHEST_POINT data source and the getter shape are also unstated. -> ADR-0019 makes chest_point(player_id) an absolute body-frame point, consistent with the same tick's pos_curr: either computed at read time from BodyView pos plus the stored offset, or derived in controller.noise. It exposes the point as two int getters and names the ADR-0007 table the sim loads CHEST_POINT from. ADR-0017 D5.3 and the ADR-0019 cross-ADR row then cite the corrected timing; ADR-0018 needs no change.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0018; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0018, ADR-0009: The Avatar Presenter places the beam Light2D at the chest point through Placement.put (ADR-0019 §7.2). ADR-0018 mode B requires the foot cell plus CELL_CENTRE through Placement.put_light_origin, with the chest offset used only for the apex. -> ADR-0019 §7.1, §7.2 and CTL-11 adopt ADR-0018's Light2D origin rule verbatim (put_light_origin at the foot cell plus CELL_CENTRE under the selected SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE; rotation stays the Presenter's); ADR-0009 F1 supplies put_light_origin.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0019; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0015: ControllerView lacks has_row(player_id), which Body needs for BDY_SEAT_UNBOUND. ADR-0019 §2.6 says Body reads intent_octant; ADR-0015 reads only octant and gait_effective. -> ADR-0019 adds get_has_row(player_id) -> bool to ControllerView and strikes intent_octant from the §2.6 list of Body's reads.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0026; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0015, ADR-0026: ADR-0019 §1.1 attributes the pod-body test (the input to IN_POD) to body.state. ADR-0015 disowns it, and ADR-0019's own assumptions put pod-body semantics on ADR-0026. -> ADR-0026 publishes an allocation-free is_pod_body(body_id) -> bool, or equivalent, on its view. ADR-0019 §1.1 and §2.4 cite it as the IN_POD input, and ADR-0015 keeps no pod predicate.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0034; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0034: ADR-0034 assumes the Avatar Presenter attaches through BodyScenes.attach_presenter(actor_id, node) at spawn and never reparents itself. ADR-0019 §7 is silent on node parenting across body transfers. -> ADR-0034 owns the attach_presenter contract and the stage-0 reparent on BODY_TRANSFER. ADR-0019 §7.1 adds one sentence adopting it.
  [from ADR-0019 review] owner ADR-0005; adrs ADR-0019, ADR-0005, ADR-0016: block_hash is taken over the normalised snapshot payload (ADR-0005 §4.3; ADR-0016 §9.1 normalise-in-snapshot), so controller.state's hash cannot see intent, gait, ramp, stagger or channel values. (a) Freeing a BodyRoot also frees every foreign node attached through BodyScenes: the Avatar Presenter, Trail, Interaction, Horror and Suit nodes. § 7.1 promises 'the projector ... never frees it', and the ADR's own Must-never forbids freeing a node another presenter attached. (b) ADR-0009 § 2 (L179) says a PROJECTOR answering ALL keeps 'drawing the last complete state until the chunks finish'. ADR-0034 instead draws nothing during the rebuild. (c) ADR-0008 shows the HoldLayer only while the kernel is LOADING, and the hold releases on RUNNING. After a load the interior is therefore empty for ceil(U / BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME) frames, up to 3 at the MVP. The ProjectorReadiness latch is read only for TRANSIT_HOLD. (d) Nothing says what happens to the foreign attachments of a section that leaves the ProjectionSet ('freed at the end of the next stage-0 pass'), or of a root freed after a cut. -> Before any root or scene is freed (restore, ALL, a ProjectionSet exit, a dissolved or dead body), body.projector reparents every foreign attachment into Staging with SceneMove.to and keeps its registration (body_id, section_id, rank, entity_id). It re-mounts each one when its body or section is mounted again, and calls a declared on_orphaned or detach notification for any whose section or body no longer exists. On restore, either keep the old roots drawing until the new set commits, as ADR-0009 § 2 requires, or ask ADR-0008 to keep the load hold until ProjectorReadiness.is_ready(); state which in § 6 and § 7. Add a validation row: after a restore, every attachment is under the right body root and OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT is unchanged.
  ADR-0034 T3: The cross-presenter access in this design is not sanctioned by ADR-0009, and § 5 contradicts itself. ADR-0009 L144: 'Presentation never reads another presenter's private state. A presenter may call a getter on a strictly earlier stage's product.' This ADR breaks that in three places. (a) BodyScenes.attach, attach_presenter and detach are mutations, called from stages 2 to 7 (Avatar, Trail and others) into a stage-0 product. (b) body.projector consumes the Layout projector's SectionScene handles, and both are stage-0 presenters. PresenterDescriptor.after only orders presenters within a stage; it does not permit one to read another's product. (c) § 5, the Implementation Guidelines and Alternative 9 say the Layout projector never builds into a body root. Yet § 7 step 5 has it build socket-state sprites 'into the still-mounted SectionScenes', and swap_in replaces nodes 'under whatever parent it is currently mounted on'. Both are writes under body.projector's roots and into its SortedLayers. The design is sound, but as written it breaks a Foundation rule and its own rule. -> Add an explicit amendment request to ADR-0009 (see cross_adr) that sanctions: (1) the Layout projector and body.projector as one PROJECTOR pair with a declared same-stage handoff object (SectionScene), with body.projector declaring after: [layout_projector]; (2) BodyScenes as a named mutation facade that later-stage presenters may call, limited to attach, detach and rebind, and never a getter of private state. In ADR-0034 § 5, restate the rule as: the Layout projector creates nodes only in Staging or through SectionScene methods; all parenting and SortedLayer insertion under a body root goes through body.projector, which can be invoked through the SectionScene. Fix the § 7 step 5 wording to match. Add the descriptor fields (reads, after) for both projectors to Key Interfaces.
  For each cross-ADR item (merge duplicates) issue ONE ruling with an id (CT-01, CT-02...), the single owner_adr that changes, the other ADRs that must align their references, and the exact amendment text. Also look for conflicts the reviewers missed between the Core ADRs (ownership of blocks and ids, interface signatures, hook order and divisors, restore order, budgets that sum past STEP_BUDGET_MS or the frame budget, dependency cycles in Depends On). If a Foundation ADR genuinely must change, list it in foundation_amendments (the orchestrator applies those separately); prefer changing the Core ADR. Reject findings that are wrong, with reasons. Read by section (whole-file reads over 40 KB are refused).

# Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag
- [Consistency-check needs a confirming run](consistency-check-confirming-run.md) — owner+registry fixes leave leftovers in consumer GDDs; grep referenced_by docs, print patch counts

  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.
